title: November 18 — WaveFormer: resonant recurrence with attention
summary: WaveFormer is an MIT-licensed new repository for testing a resonant recurrent attention-head replacement. At registration it contains only a license: no implementation, training run, or performance advantage. Qwenimagination's V2/V3 concept transfer is real but later persistent-write tests remain negative.

nodes.claim: New experimental repo proposed to compare a tiny transformer's attention head with damped resonant recurrence and non-oscillatory recurrent controls, at matched compute.
nodes.survived: The repo exists under an MIT license; its implementation and experimental result are pending.
nodes.killed: At registration only the license is committed. No model or outcome exists, and earlier wave-relais often underperform scalar baselines.

edges.why: Off-token concept transfer motivates a learned recurrent read/write interface, but there is no shared implementation.
The two-form content/prediction distinction informs a proposed resonant head; waves have not yet earned a numerical advantage.
Distributed persistent context motivates future local gates, not yet implemented in WaveFormer.

motifs.title: Precise attention alongside persistent recurrent state
motifs.description: Proposed learned resonant recurrence compared with ordinary attention and a nonoscillatory recurrent control; no outcome yet.
